description: Replace an always-allow stub with a token bucket that refills fractionally over elapsed time and caps at capacity
prompts: limiter.rb's TokenBucket#allow always returns true. Implement it properly: TokenBucket.new(capacity, refill_rate) - `refill_rate` tokens are added per second, capped at `capacity` tokens (never above it, even after a long idle period). allow(now) refills the bucket based on elapsed seconds since the last call, then - if at least 1 token is available - consumes exactly 1 token and returns true; otherwise returns false and consumes nothing. The bucket starts full at construction time.
name: add_ruby_token_bucket_limiter

test_setup_files.limiter_hidden_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "limiter"

class TokenBucketTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_starts_full_and_drains
    b = TokenBucket.new(3, 1)
    assert b.allow(0)
    assert b.allow(0)
    assert b.allow(0)
    refute b.allow(0)
  end

  def test_refills_over_time
    b = TokenBucket.new(3, 1)
    3.times { b.allow(0) }
    refute b.allow(0.5)
    assert b.allow(1.0)
    refute b.allow(1.0)
  end

  def test_refill_caps_at_capacity
    b = TokenBucket.new(2, 1)
    b.allow(0)
    b.allow(0)
    assert b.allow(1000)
    assert b.allow(1000)
    refute b.allow(1000)
  end
end
